Process analytics for your golf

The truth about your game.Your round is a process. Measure it like one.

Your score is the output; every shot is a step in the process. Golfimbul applies the process analytics that run world-class operations to your golf: it separates real change from noise, finds the step where your strokes leak, and proves when a fix worked. Every shot, logged in five minutes.

Built by a golfer, for golfers. Not by developers or statisticians who don't play — by a golfer who improves processes for a living, logs every round, and applied the same method to his own game.
Your game, round by roundcontrol chart

Your score is a consequence of your process. The control chart watches the process — and tells you exactly when it changed, and that it stuck.

One great round proves nothing. Neither does a bad one. The only way to be sure you're getting better is to see your game change — and stay changed.

Powerful

An analytical approach no other golf app has.

Other apps give you more numbers. Golfimbul gives you a method: the process control used by the best-run businesses in the world to tell a real change from random variation — applied to your game.

What other golf apps show you

The trend line points down, six strokes better. You'd celebrate, or decide your new swing works. Nothing in this chart can tell you it's luck.

What Golfimbul shows you

The same rounds. Every one sits inside the limits drawn from your own history, and no pattern has formed. The good run at the end is your normal on good days — nothing has changed yet. Keep working: the day it's real, the chart will say so.

And the opposite mistake: you did improve, and nothing told you.

What other golf apps show you

Your average has not moved and your last five rounds are slightly worse, with an 11-over among them. You'd conclude the work isn't paying off and change something that was working. Nothing in this chart can tell you that you already improved.

What Golfimbul shows you

The same rounds. Eight in a row better than your old average is not luck: your level moved from +7.3 to +5.0, more than two strokes. The +11 and the +8 at the end sit inside your new limits: a bad day at your new level, not a relapse. You improved, and now you know it.

Real change vs. a good week

Every stat gets limits drawn from your own history. When something moves outside them, you know it is real — and the app re-baselines from there.

Where the strokes go

Strokes gained for every shot, the five mistakes that cost amateurs the most, and what actually drives your score — measured against your handicap, not a tour pro.

What to practise next

Not twenty charts. One priority, ranked by strokes on the table. Fix it, watch the chart confirm it, move to the next.

Strategy

Stats that change how you play — and how you improve.

Stats should not be static. On the course, they decide which club, which target, which number to leave yourself, where to miss. Off the course, they decide what you practise — and tell you whether it worked.

How you play

Aim where your miss is safe

Your bag shows where each club really finishes — short, long, left, right. Pick targets that forgive the miss you actually have, not the shot you wish you had.

Lay up to your best number

Strokes gained by distance and lie shows the yardages you score from and the ones that cost you. Leave yourself the first, avoid the second.

Take the big number off the table

The Tiger's 5 shows which mistakes keep showing up — doubles, 3-putts, bogeys with a short iron in hand. Change the plan that leads to them, not just the swing.

How you improve

Practise where the strokes are

Strokes gained splits every round into tee, approach, short game and putting. The biggest negative is where an hour of practice buys the most strokes — not the part of your game you enjoy hitting.

Know if the change worked

Changed your putting routine? A good round proves nothing. The control chart tells you when the numbers really moved — or that it was just a good day, so you don't throw away what works.

One priority at a time

Your priorities rank the leaks by strokes. Fix the first one until the chart shows it, then move to the next. Improvement is a process, not a mood.

No shortcuts

No data, no truth.

Golfimbul does not guess. It tells you what your own rounds show, so what you get grows with what you log. Anyone who promises you analysis from one round is selling you noise.

Phone or laptop?

Best on your laptop.

We recommend using Golfimbul on a computer, in your browser: a bigger screen and a real keyboard make logging and reading your charts faster. If you insist on using your phone, there is an app you can install from this site.

About us

Built by a golfer, for golfers.

Golfimbul was created by Guido Sargiotto, an industrial engineer and amateur golfer from Córdoba, Argentina. His work is helping businesses find where their processes lose value — and proving, with control charts, when a change really worked.

It started as a spreadsheet for his own rounds, then for a few friends. It became an app when it was clear the same question kept coming back: am I really getting better?

The name comes from an old tale: in Tolkien's The Hobbit, a well-struck blow sends Golfimbul flying into a rabbit hole — and, so the story goes, the game of golf is invented. The first hole. The first real change.

Stop guessing. Start seeing.

◎ What drives your score

05 Scoring trend

Everything above adds up to this — your score to par, round by round, on control-chart footing. Below zero is the goal; lower is better, so a point below the lower limit is a breakthrough round and one above the upper limit is a blow-up. Whenever a signal fires the limits recalculate, so each stable stretch is judged against its own baseline.
